source_note.authority: Common Core State Standards Initiative, official thecorestandards.org mathematics pages
source_note.verification_method: The research agent fetched each selected individual standard page and checked the excerpt against returned page text. The parent saved the verified excerpts; no model generation was performed during source verification.
source_note.timestamp_note: The date identifies this experiment session. Independent HTTP request timestamps were unavailable; no exact retrieval time is claimed.
source_note.text_policy: Contiguous official excerpts, with presentation-only italic markup removed. Partial sentences and clauses are identified in case verification notes. Labels and notes are assistant-authored.
source_note.coverage_policy: Selected prerequisite anchors, not complete coverage of every teacher stipulation or evidence of actual learner knowledge. Uncovered skills and representation permissions remain hypothetical teacher assumptions. Target-method instruction is not assumed.
retrieval_issues: Some domain landing pages returned only titles; selected individual standard pages provided the quoted text.
Discovery URLs /Math/Content/4/OA/A/5/ and /Math/Content/7/SP/A/5/ returned 404 pages. The correct /Math/Content/4/OA/C/5/ and /Math/Content/7/SP/C/5/ pages were successfully verified.
No selected excerpt depends on a failed request.
source_note.adapter_limit: Only source_url, standard_id, label and text are forwarded as D1 evidence. Verification and coverage notes are audit metadata, not extra learner knowledge.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: fractions formed from equal parts of a whole
grounding_evidence.text: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: whole-number division as equal sharing and grouping
grounding_evidence.text: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

fraction_equivalence.verification: 3.NF.A.1 is complete; 3.OA.A.2 is its first sentence. Both were verified at the listed official URLs. Fraction diagram conventions remain stipulated. Whole-number sharing is not evidence of every fractional-sharing skill. Equivalence instruction is deliberately excluded.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: simple equivalent fractions explained with visual models
grounding_evidence.text: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3. Explain why the fractions are equivalent, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: fraction addition with like denominators and a common whole
grounding_evidence.text: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

fraction_addition.verification: Both complete substandards were verified at the listed official URLs. Visual equivalence and same-denominator addition are stipulated prerequisites, not an assumed general unlike-denominator algorithm. Diagram format and fluency remain hypothetical teacher stipulations.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: whole-number division interpreted as grouping
grounding_evidence.text: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: multiplication involving fractions
grounding_evidence.text: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: unit fractions represented on a number line
grounding_evidence.text: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.

fraction_division.verification: Official URLs verified. 3.OA.A.2 is its first sentence; the other excerpts are complete. The number-line excerpt covers unit fractions, not every fraction diagram. Neither unit-fraction division nor general fraction division is assumed as taught.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: equal grouping and division
grounding_evidence.text: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: basic ratio concepts and ratio language
grounding_evidence.text: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: a fraction of a whole-number quantity
grounding_evidence.text: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.

ratio_sharing.verification: First sentences verified at all three official URLs. Fraction-of-quantity support is scoped to whole numbers. Converting part-to-part ratios into fractions of a shared total remains the target, not prior knowledge.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: percent as a rate per hundred and percent of a quantity
grounding_evidence.text: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: decimal arithmetic to hundredths
grounding_evidence.text: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

percentage_change.verification: Complete official excerpts verified. Decimal fluency beyond hundredths is not established. Changing reference quantities and noncancellation of equal percentage increases and decreases remain for exploration.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: interpreting unit rates
grounding_evidence.text: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: arithmetic with decimals to hundredths
grounding_evidence.text: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and/or the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate the strategy to a written method and explain the reasoning used.

proportionality.verification: 6.RP.A.2 first sentence and complete 5.NBT.B.7 verified. Generic two-column-table reading and the full integer-arithmetic repertoire remain teacher stipulations. No proportionality-classification criterion is assumed.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: solving individual one-variable linear equations
grounding_evidence.text: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: plotting and interpreting coordinate points
grounding_evidence.text: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

linear_systems.verification: 7.EE.B.4.a first two sentences and complete 5.G.A.2 verified. Trial-and-check tables remain stipulated; plotting beyond the first quadrant is not grounded. A common solution satisfying two conditions remains the target.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: one-step equations with nonnegative rational numbers
grounding_evidence.text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all nonnegative rational numbers.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: numerical comparisons on a number line
grounding_evidence.text: Interpret statements of inequality as statements about the relative position of two numbers on a number line diagram.

inequalities.verification: Complete 6.EE.B.7 and first sentence of 6.NS.C.7.a verified. Equations are scoped to nonnegative rational numbers. Numerical ordering does not assume instruction in variable inequalities or feasible sets.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: unit rates as existing rate knowledge
grounding_evidence.text: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0, and use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: plotting and interpreting points in context
grounding_evidence.text: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

linear_growth.verification: 6.RP.A.2 first sentence and complete 5.G.A.2 verified. Reading tables and additional graphing conventions remain stipulated. All-quadrant plotting is not grounded. Formal slope and rate versus starting amount remain the target.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: generating number or shape patterns from a given rule
grounding_evidence.text: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule itself.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: recording operations with numerical and letter expressions
grounding_evidence.text: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and with letters standing for numbers.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: multiplication and rectangular area
grounding_evidence.text: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

quadratic_patterns.verification: 4.OA.C.5 first two sentences, 6.EE.A.2.a first sentence and complete 3.MD.C.7.b verified. Given-rule pattern activity does not assume unknown quadratic-rule discovery. Visual-pattern conventions and full linear-expression fluency remain stipulated. Area support is whole-number scoped.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: rectangle area from side-length multiplication
grounding_evidence.text: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: existing rectangle area and perimeter formulas
grounding_evidence.text: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.

area_perimeter.verification: Complete 3.MD.C.7.b and first sentence of 4.MD.A.3 verified. Arbitrary-polygon perimeter and grid drawing are not fully grounded. The standard explicitly describing equal perimeter with different areas is excluded.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: equivalent-ratio tables
grounding_evidence.text: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: triangle and polygon areas through composition and decomposition
grounding_evidence.text: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

similarity_scaling.verification: Both complete official excerpts verified. Geometric length-scale factors remain specifically teacher-stipulated; whole-number ratio tables provide partial support only. Scale-drawing standards already requiring scaled-area computation are excluded.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: rectangular and square areas as products
grounding_evidence.text: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: evaluating whole-number exponents
grounding_evidence.text: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: coordinate points in the first quadrant
grounding_evidence.text: Represent real world and mathematical problems by graphing points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane, and interpret coordinate values of points in the context of the situation.

pythagorean_distance.verification: All three complete official excerpts verified. Squares are a rectangle special case. Measuring, drawing lengths and square-root repertoire remain stipulated, not directly grounded. Coordinate support covers the first quadrant only. Pythagorean and diagonal-distance instruction is excluded.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: existing rectangle, triangle, and polygon area reasoning
grounding_evidence.text: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles and other shapes; apply these techniques in the context of solving real-world and mathematical problems.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: measuring area by counting unit squares
grounding_evidence.text: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft, and improvised units).

circle_area.verification: Both complete official excerpts verified. Radius/diameter terminology and partial-square estimation remain teacher stipulations. The circle-area standard is excluded because it assumes the target formula.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: existing volume formulas for rectangular prisms
grounding_evidence.text: Apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms to find volumes of right rectangular prisms with whole-number edge lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: existing rectangle-area calculation
grounding_evidence.text: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles with whole-number side lengths in the context of solving real world and mathematical problems, and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas in mathematical reasoning.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: representing three-dimensional figures using nets
grounding_evidence.text: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made up of rectangles and triangles

volume_surface.verification: First two excerpts are complete; 6.G.A.4 is the exact opening clause ending before the comma, deliberately omitting its surface-area instruction. All official URLs verified. Volume/area support is whole-number scoped. Particular box-net layout remains stipulated. Equal-volume comparisons and optimization remain the target.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: elementary probability and likelihood
grounding_evidence.text: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: existing uniform probability models in simple-event contexts
grounding_evidence.text: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: fractions built from equal-sized parts
grounding_evidence.text: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.

sample_space.verification: 7.SP.C.5 and 3.NF.A.1 are complete; 7.SP.C.7.a is its first sentence. Official URLs verified. Uniform models are used only as stipulated simple-event knowledge. Lists/two-way tables remain stipulated. Named compound outcomes are not automatically equiprobable; compound-event instruction is excluded.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: simple uniform probability models
grounding_evidence.text: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: percentages as fractions per hundred
grounding_evidence.text: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

conditional_probability.verification: 7.SP.C.7.a first sentence and complete 6.RP.A.3.c verified. Two-way-count-table reading remains stipulated; general fraction fluency is only partially anchored. Population restriction and conditional probability remain targets, not prior instruction.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: elementary percent calculations
grounding_evidence.text: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: reporting observation counts
grounding_evidence.text: Reporting the number of observations.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: using tables to compare ratios
grounding_evidence.text: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.

sampling_bias.verification: All complete official excerpts verified. Survey display conventions remain stipulated. Reporting counts and comparing ratios do not establish random-sampling, representativeness or bias knowledge. The sampling-representativeness standard is excluded.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: existing mean as a measure of center
grounding_evidence.text: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean)

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: multiplication and division within 100
grounding_evidence.text: Fluently multiply and divide within 100, using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division (e.g., knowing that 8 × 5 = 40, one knows 40 ÷ 5 = 8) or properties of operations.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: observation counts as existing data information
grounding_evidence.text: Reporting the number of observations.

weighted_mean.verification: 6.SP.B.5.c is its exact opening clause, omitting variability/distribution text; 3.OA.C.7 is its first sentence; 6.SP.B.5.a is complete. All URLs verified. Mean computation and group-size-table reading remain teacher stipulations. Arithmetic beyond 100 is not fully grounded. Combining unequal groups remains the target.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: interpreting scatter plots for association
grounding_evidence.text: interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities.

grounding_evidence.label: CCSS: existing means as measures of center
grounding_evidence.text: Giving quantitative measures of center (median and/or mean)

correlation_causation.verification: 8.SP.A.1 is the exact first-sentence clause following 'Construct and'; 6.SP.B.5.c is the exact opening clause. Both official URLs verified. Group-average comparisons and everyday data descriptions remain stipulated beyond the mean anchor. The correlation-versus-causation standard is excluded.
